title.en: Volume 25 Later Tang Biographies 5: Zhou Dewei, Fu Cunshen, Shi Jiantang, Wang Jianji, Yuan Xingqin, An Jinquan, Yuan Jianfeng, Xi Fangye
title.raw: 卷二十五 唐臣傳第十三: 周德威 符存審 史建瑭 王建及 元行欽 安金全 袁建豐 西方鄴 Volume 25 Later Tang Biographies 5: Zhou Dewei, Fu Cunshen, Shi Jiantang, Wang Jianji, Yuan Xingqin, An Jinquan, Yuan Jianfeng, Xi Fangye

sentences.zh: 周德威

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei

sentences.zh: 周德威，字鎮遠，朔州馬邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei, styled Zhenyuan, was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei, styled Zhenyuan, came from Mayi in Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 為人勇而多智，能望塵以知敵數。

translations.literal: As a man he was brave and full of stratagem, able to tell an enemy’s numbers from the dust they raised.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and cunning, he could read an enemy’s strength from the dust on the horizon.

sentences.zh: 其狀貌雄偉，笑不改容，人見之，凜如也。

translations.literal: His appearance was imposing; even when he smiled his bearing did not soften, and those who saw him felt a chill.
translations.idiomatic: He was a towering figure; his smile never softened his face, and men who met him felt a cold dread.

sentences.zh: 事晉王為騎將，稍遷鐵林軍使，從破王行瑜，以功遷衙內指揮使。

translations.literal: He served the Prince of Jin as a mounted officer, was gradually promoted to commander of the Iron Forest Army, followed in the defeat of Wang Xingyu, and for merit was transferred to Inner Gate director of command.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Prince of Jin’s service as a cavalry officer, rose to command the Iron Forest Army, helped break Wang Xingyu, and was made Inner Gate director of command for his deeds.

sentences.zh: 其小字陽五，當梁、晉之際，周陽五之勇聞天下。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Yangwu; in the era when Liang and Jin contended, the courage of Zhou Yangwu was known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Men called him Yangwu as a boy; in the wars between Liang and Jin, the name Zhou Yangwu rang across the empire.

sentences.zh: 梁軍圍晉太原，令軍中曰：「能生得周陽五者為刺史。

translations.literal: When Liang besieged Taiyuan of Jin, they proclaimed in the army: “Whoever can capture Zhou Yangwu alive shall be made regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang encircled Jin’s Taiyuan, the command went out: “Take Zhou Yangwu alive and you shall be made regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 」有驍將陳章者，號陳野義，常乘白馬被朱甲以自異，出入陣中，求周陽五，欲必生致之。

translations.literal: ” There was a fierce general named Chen Zhang, called Chen Yeyi, who often rode a white horse and wore vermilion armor to distinguish himself; he moved in and out of the battle lines seeking Zhou Yangwu, determined to take him alive.
translations.idiomatic: ” One of their champions, Chen Zhang—called Chen Yeyi—marked himself with a white horse and vermilion mail and ranged the field hunting Zhou Yangwu, sworn to bring him in alive.

sentences.zh: 晉王戒德威曰：「陳野義欲得汝以求刺史，見白馬朱甲者，宜善備之！

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin warned Dewei: “Chen Yeyi wants you to win the inspectorate—when you see white horse and vermilion armor, you must guard against him well!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin warned Dewei: “Chen Yeyi means to earn his prefecture with your capture—when you see white horse and red armor, be on your guard!

sentences.zh: 」德威笑曰：「陳章好大言耳，安知刺史非臣作邪？

translations.literal: ” Dewei laughed and said: “Chen Zhang loves big talk—how does he know the inspectorate won’t be mine?
translations.idiomatic: ” Dewei laughed. “Chen Zhang is all boast—who says the prefecture is not already mine?

sentences.zh: 」因戒其部兵曰：「見白馬朱甲者，當佯走以避之。

translations.literal: ” He then warned his troops: “When you see white horse and vermilion armor, feign flight to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he told his men: “See white horse and red armor—fall back as if routed.

sentences.zh: 」兩軍皆陣，德威微服雜卒伍中。

translations.literal: ” Both armies drew up in formation; Dewei put on plain clothes and mingled among the rank and file.
translations.idiomatic: ” Both hosts formed up. Dewei shed his insignia and stood among the common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 陳章出挑戰，兵始交，德威部下見白馬朱甲者，因退走，章果奮槊急追之，德威伺章已過，揮鐵槌擊之，中章墮馬，遂生擒之。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang came out to challenge battle; as the troops first engaged, Dewei’s men, seeing the white horse and vermilion armor, withdrew in flight; Zhang indeed charged fiercely in pursuit with his lance; Dewei waited until Zhang had passed, swung his iron mace and struck him; it hit Zhang and he fell from his horse, and they captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang rode out to fight. At the first clash Dewei’s men spotted the white horse and red mail and broke as ordered. Zhang drove his lance in hard pursuit—then Dewei, letting him pass, swung his iron mace and knocked him from the saddle. They took him alive.

sentences.zh: 梁攻燕，晉遣德威將五萬人為燕攻梁，取潞州，遷代州刺史、內外蕃漢馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Liang attacked Yan, Jin sent Dewei with fifty thousand men to aid Yan against Liang; he took Luzhou, was transferred to prefect of Dai, and made overall commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang struck Yan, Jin sent Dewei with fifty thousand to help Yan turn on Liang. He seized Luzhou, became prefect of Dai, and was named overall commander of all barbarian and Han horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 梁軍舍燕攻潞，圍以夾城，潞州守將李嗣昭閉城拒守，而德威與梁軍相持於外逾年。

translations.literal: Liang abandoned Yan to attack Luzhou and besieged it with twin fortifications; the Luzhou defender Li Sizhao shut the gates and held firm, while Dewei faced the Liang army outside for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Liang left Yan and turned on Luzhou, ringed it with twin siege lines, and Li Sizhao held the city while Dewei held the field more than a year.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭與德威素有隙，晉王病且革，語莊宗曰：「梁軍圍潞，而德威與嗣昭有隙，吾甚憂之！

translations.literal: Sizhao and Dewei had long been at odds; the Prince of Jin lay gravely ill and told Zhuangzong: “Liang besieges Luzhou, and Dewei and Sizhao are estranged—I am deeply troubled!
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao and Dewei had never been friends. The Prince of Jin, dying, told Zhuangzong: “Liang has Luzhou pinned, and Dewei and Sizhao are at odds—I fear what may come.

sentences.zh: 」王喪在殯，莊宗新立，殺其叔父克寧，國中未定，而晉之重兵，悉屬德威於外，晉人皆恐。

translations.literal: ” While the king’s body still lay in state, Zhuangzong had just succeeded and executed his uncle Kening; the realm was unsettled, and Jin’s main force all belonged to Dewei in the field; the people of Jin were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: ” The coffin had barely been set out when Zhuangzong took the throne, killed his uncle Kening, and left the state unsteady. Jin’s best troops were all with Dewei abroad, and every heart in Taiyuan trembled.

sentences.zh: 莊宗使人以喪及克寧之難告德威，且召其軍。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong sent men to tell Dewei of the mourning and Kening’s disaster, and also summoned his army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent word of the mourning and Kening’s fall, and called Dewei’s army home.

sentences.zh: 德威聞命，即日還軍太原，留其兵城外，徒步而入，伏梓宮前慟哭幾絕，晉人乃安。

translations.literal: On hearing the order, Dewei that same day returned his army to Taiyuan, left his troops outside the walls, entered on foot, prostrated himself before the coffin and wept until he nearly died; only then did the people of Jin feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei obeyed at once, marched to Taiyuan, camped his men outside the walls, and walked in alone. He threw himself before the coffin and wept until he nearly fainted—and only then did Jin breathe easy.

sentences.zh: 遂從莊宗復擊梁軍，破夾城，與李嗣昭歡如初。

translations.literal: He then followed Zhuangzong in a renewed attack on the Liang army, broke the twin fortifications, and he and Li Sizhao were close again as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong back to the field, smashed the twin lines, and he and Li Sizhao were friends again as before.

sentences.zh: 以破夾城功，拜振武節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: For breaking the twin fortifications he was made military governor of Zhenwu and co-equal grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: For breaking the twin fortifications he was made military governor of Zhenwu and co-equal grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 天祐七年秋，梁遣王景仁將魏、滑、汴、宋等兵七萬人擊趙。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianyou, Liang sent Wang Jingren with troops from Wei, Hua, Bian, and Song—seventy thousand men—to attack Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Tianyou 7 (910), Liang sent Wang Jingren with seventy thousand men from Wei, Hua, Bian, and Song against Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙王王熔乞師於晉，晉遣德威先屯趙州。

translations.literal: The Zhao king Wang Rong begged Jin for troops; Jin sent Dewei to encamp first at Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Zhao pleaded for aid; Jin sent Dewei to hold Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬，梁軍至柏鄉，趙人告急，莊宗自將出贊皇，會德威於石橋，進距柏鄉五里，營於野河北。

translations.literal: In winter the Liang army reached Baixiang; Zhao sent urgent word; Zhuangzong personally led the army out through Zanhuang, joined Dewei at Shiqiao, advanced to within five li of Baixiang, and encamped north of the Wild River.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Liang reached Baixiang. Zhao cried for help. Zhuangzong marched out through Zanhuang, met Dewei at Stone Bridge, pushed to within five li of Baixiang, and camped north of the Wild River.

sentences.zh: 晉兵少，而景仁所將神威、龍驤、拱宸等軍，皆梁精兵，人馬鎧甲飾以組繡金銀，其光耀日，晉軍望之色動。

translations.literal: Jin troops were few, while the armies Jingren led—Divine Might, Dragon Soar, and Bent Bow—were all Liang’s elite; men, horses, armor, and trappings were adorned with brocade, gold, and silver, shining in the sun; the Jin army gazed on them and their color changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was badly outnumbered. Jingren’s Divine Might, Dragon Soar, and Bent Bow corps were Liang’s flower—mail and harness bright with brocade, gold, and silver, flashing in the sun. Jin soldiers looked and lost heart.

sentences.zh: 德威勉其眾曰：「此汴、宋傭販兒，徒飾其外耳，其中不足懼也！

translations.literal: Dewei urged his men: “These are Bian and Song peddlers—only their outsides are dressed up; within, there is nothing to fear!
translations.idiomatic: Dewei rallied his men: “These Bian and Song shop boys dress the part—inside the armor there is nothing to fear!

sentences.zh: 其一甲直數十千，擒之適足為吾資，無徒望而愛之，當勉以往取之。

translations.literal: One suit of armor is worth tens of thousands; capture it and it becomes our prize—do not stand gazing and loving it; press forward and take it.
translations.idiomatic: Each suit costs tens of thousands—take one and it pays our march. Do not stand admiring their glitter; go and strip it from them.

sentences.zh: 」退而告莊宗曰：「梁兵甚銳，未可與爭，宜少退以待之。

translations.literal: ” He withdrew and told Zhuangzong: “Liang’s troops are very sharp; we cannot fight them yet—we should pull back a little and wait.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then told Zhuangzong in private: “Liang is too sharp for a straight fight. Pull back and let them come to us.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「吾提孤軍出千里，其利速戰。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong said: “I have led a lone army a thousand li—my advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong said: “I marched a thousand li with this lone host—speed is our edge.

sentences.zh: 今不乘勢急擊之，使敵知吾之眾寡，則吾無所施矣！

translations.literal: If we do not seize the moment and strike hard, and let the enemy learn our numbers, we will have nowhere to act!
translations.idiomatic: If we wait and let them count our ranks, we lose every opening we have!

sentences.zh: 」德威曰：「不然，趙人能城守而不能野戰。

translations.literal: ” Dewei said: “Not so—the people of Zhao can hold cities but cannot fight in the open.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dewei said: “No. Zhao can man walls, not open fields.

sentences.zh: 吾之取勝，利在騎兵，平川廣野，騎兵之所長也。

translations.literal: Our victory depends on cavalry; on level plain and broad wild, cavalry is what we do best.
translations.idiomatic: We win on horse. Broad plain and open ground—that is where cavalry shines.

sentences.zh: 今吾軍於河上，迫賊營門，非吾用長之地也。

translations.literal: Now our army is on the river, pressed against the enemy camp gate—that is not ground where our strength applies.
translations.idiomatic: Here we sit on the riverbank under their gate—that is not country where we can use our strength.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗不悅，退臥帳中，諸將無敢入見。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong was displeased, withdrew and lay in his tent, and none of the generals dared enter to see him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong turned away displeased, lay down in his tent, and no general dared go in.

sentences.zh: 德威謂監軍張承業曰：「王怒老兵。

translations.literal: Dewei told the army monitor Zhang Chengye: “The king is angry with this old soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei told the army monitor Zhang Chengye: “The king is furious with this old soldier.

sentences.zh: 不速戰者，非怯也。

translations.literal: Refusing swift battle is not cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Holding back is not fear.

sentences.zh: 且吾兵少而臨賊營門，所恃者，一水隔耳。

translations.literal: Our troops are few and we face the enemy camp gate; all we rely on is a strip of water between us.
translations.idiomatic: We are too few to sit under their walls. One river is all that shields us.

sentences.zh: 使梁得舟筏渡河，吾無類矣！

translations.literal: If Liang gets boats and rafts across the river, we are finished!
translations.idiomatic: If Liang ferries across, we are done for!

sentences.zh: 不如退軍鄗邑，誘敵出營，擾而勞之，可以策勝也。

translations.literal: Better to withdraw the army to Haoyi, lure the enemy out of camp, harass and wear them down—then we can win by plan.
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw to Haoyi, draw them out, harry and tire them—that is how we win.

sentences.zh: 」承業入言曰：「德威老將知兵，願無忽其言！

translations.literal: ” Chengye entered and said: “Dewei is an old general who knows war—please do not ignore his words!
translations.idiomatic: ” Chengye went in and said: “Dewei is a veteran who knows war—do not dismiss him!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗遽起曰：「吾方思之耳。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong rose at once and said: “I was just thinking the same.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong sat up at once. “I was thinking the same thing.

sentences.zh: 」已而德威獲梁遊兵，問景仁何為，曰：「治舟數百，將以為浮梁。

translations.literal: ” Before long Dewei captured a Liang patrol and asked what Jingren was doing; he said: “He is preparing several hundred boats to make a floating bridge.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Dewei took a Liang scout and asked Jingren’s plan. “He is building hundreds of boats for a pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 」德威引與俱見，莊宗笑曰：「果如公所料。

translations.literal: ” Dewei brought him in to see Zhuangzong together; Zhuangzong laughed and said: “It is exactly as you foresaw.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dewei brought the man before Zhuangzong, who laughed: “Just as you said.

sentences.zh: 」乃退軍鄗邑。

translations.literal: ” They then withdrew the army to Haoyi.
translations.idiomatic: ” They pulled back to Haoyi.

sentences.zh: 德威晨遣三百騎叩梁營挑戰，自以勁兵三千繼之。

translations.literal: At dawn Dewei sent three hundred horsemen to strike the Liang camp in challenge, and himself followed with three thousand crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Dewei sent three hundred riders to taunt the Liang camp, then followed with three thousand picked men.

sentences.zh: 景仁怒，悉其軍以出，與德威轉鬥數十里，至於鄗南。

translations.literal: Jingren in anger brought out his whole army; he and Dewei fought in running battle for several tens of li, reaching south of Haoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingren in fury marched out with his whole host. He and Dewei skirmished for miles until they reached south of Haoyi.

sentences.zh: 兩軍皆陣，梁軍橫亙六七里，汴、宋之軍居西，魏、滑之軍居東。

translations.literal: Both armies drew up in formation; the Liang line stretched six or seven li; the Bian and Song troops were on the west, the Wei and Hua troops on the east.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides formed. Liang’s line ran six or seven li—Bian and Song on the west, Wei and Hua on the east.

sentences.zh: 莊宗策馬登高，望而喜曰：「平原淺草，可前可卻，真吾之勝地！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong spurred his horse up a height, looked out, and said with pleasure: “Level plain and shallow grass—we can advance and withdraw; this is truly ground where we can win!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong rode to a rise, looked out, and smiled: “Open grass and flat ground—room to press and room to pull back. This is our country!

sentences.zh: 」乃使人告德威曰：「吾當為公先，公可繼進。

translations.literal: ” He then sent word to Dewei: “I will go first for you—you may follow after.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent word to Dewei: “I will lead—you follow.

sentences.zh: 」德威諫曰：「梁軍輕出而遠來，與吾轉戰，其來必不暇賫糧糗，縱其能賫亦不暇食，不及日午，人馬俱饑，因其將退而擊之勝。

translations.literal: ” Dewei remonstrated: “Liang’s army came out lightly and from far away; after fighting us in running battle they surely had no time to carry provisions—even if they carried them they had no time to eat; before noon men and horses will both be hungry; strike as they are about to withdraw and we will win.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dewei urged caution: “Liang marched out rash and far. After this running fight they cannot have full rations—even if they brought food they have not eaten. By midday men and horses will starve. Hit them as they pull back and we win.

sentences.zh: 」諸將亦皆以為然。

translations.literal: ” The other generals all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The other commanders agreed.

sentences.zh: 至未申時，梁軍東偏塵起，德威鼓噪而進，麾其西偏曰：「魏、滑軍走矣！

translations.literal: Before mid-afternoon dust rose on Liang’s eastern wing; Dewei advanced with drums and shouts, and waved to his western wing: “The Wei and Hua army is fleeing!
translations.idiomatic: Before mid-afternoon dust billowed on Liang’s east. Dewei charged with drums and cries and signaled west: “Wei and Hua are running!

sentences.zh: 」又麾其東偏曰：「梁軍走矣！

translations.literal: ” He also waved to his eastern wing: “The Liang army is fleeing!
translations.idiomatic: ” He signaled east: “Liang is running!

sentences.zh: 」梁陣動，不可復整，乃皆走，遂大敗。

translations.literal: The Liang formation shook, could no longer hold, and all fled; they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s lines buckled, broke, and ran. The rout was total.

sentences.zh: 自高阝追至於柏鄉，橫屍數十里，景仁以十餘騎僅而免。

translations.literal: They pursued from Gaoyi to Baixiang; corpses lay strewn for several tens of li; Jingren escaped with barely more than ten horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The chase ran from Gaoyi to Baixiang, dead heaped for miles. Jingren escaped with a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 自梁與晉爭，凡數十戰，其大敗未嘗如此。

translations.literal: From Liang’s contention with Jin through several tens of battles, they had never suffered defeat like this.
translations.idiomatic: In decades of war between Liang and Jin, Liang had never been broken like this.

sentences.zh: 劉守光僭號於燕，晉遣德威將三萬出飛狐以擊之。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang declared himself emperor in Yan; Jin sent Dewei with thirty thousand men out through Flying Fox to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang made himself emperor of Yan, Jin sent Dewei with thirty thousand through Flying Fox Pass.

sentences.zh: 德威入祁溝關，取涿州，遂圍守光於幽州，破其外城，守光閉門距守。

translations.literal: Dewei entered Qigou Pass, took Zhuo prefecture, then besieged Shouguang in Youzhou, broke the outer city, and Shouguang shut the gates and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei forced Qigou Pass, took Zhuo, and penned Shouguang in Youzhou. The outer city fell; Shouguang barred the inner gates.

sentences.zh: 而晉軍盡下燕諸州縣，獨幽州不下，圍之逾年乃破之，以功拜盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: Jin troops then took all Yan’s prefectures and counties; only Youzhou would not fall; they besieged it more than a year before it broke; for merit he was made military governor of the Lulong army.
translations.idiomatic: Jin swept Yan’s prefectures and counties; only Youzhou held out more than a year before it fell. For that he was made military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 德威雖為大將，而常身與士卒馳騁矢石之間。

translations.literal: Though Dewei was a great general, he often personally ranged with his soldiers amid flying arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Though a field marshal, he still rode with his men under arrow and stone.

sentences.zh: 守光驍將單廷珪，望見德威於陣，曰：「此周陽五也！

translations.literal: Shouguang’s fierce general Shan Tinggui, seeing Dewei in the formation, said: “That is Zhou Yangwu!
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tinggui, one of Shouguang’s champions, spotted Dewei in the line and cried: “There is Zhou Yangwu!

sentences.zh: 」乃挺槍馳騎追之。

translations.literal: ” He then levelled his lance and spurred in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: ” He lowered his lance and galloped after him.

sentences.zh: 德威佯走，度廷珪垂及，側身少卻，廷珪馬方馳，不可止，縱其少過，奮槌擊之，廷珪墜馬，遂見擒。

translations.literal: Dewei feigned flight; when Tinggui was almost upon him he turned slightly aside; Tinggui’s horse was at full gallop and could not stop; Dewei let him pass a little, then swung his mace and struck; Tinggui fell from his horse and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei pretended to flee. As Tinggui closed he sidestepped; the horse could not check its speed. Dewei let him pass, swung his mace, and knocked him from the saddle. They took him alive.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與劉掞相持於魏，掞夜潛軍出黃澤關以襲太原，德威自幽州以千騎入土門以躡之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and Liu Yan faced each other at Wei; Yan by night secretly marched out through Huangze Pass to strike Taiyuan; Dewei came from Youzhou with a thousand horsemen through Tumen Pass to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong and Liu Yan faced off at Wei, Yan stole out by night through Huangze Pass to hit Taiyuan. Dewei came from Youzhou with a thousand riders through Tumen Pass to trail him.

sentences.zh: 掞至樂平，遇雨不得進而還。

translations.literal: Yan reached Leeping, met rain, could not advance, and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan reached Leeping, rain stopped him, and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 德威與掞俱東，爭趨臨清。

translations.literal: Dewei and Yan both went east, racing for Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei and Yan both raced east for Linqing.

sentences.zh: 臨清有積粟，且晉軍餉道也，德威先馳據之，以故莊宗卒能困掞軍而敗之。

translations.literal: Linqing held stored grain and was also Jin’s supply route; Dewei galloped ahead and seized it first; for that reason Zhuangzong was finally able to pin Yan’s army and defeat it.
translations.idiomatic: Linqing held grain stores and fed Jin’s line of march. Dewei got there first—and because of that Zhuangzong was able to trap Yan and break him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗勇而好戰，尤銳於見敵。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was bold and loved battle, especially eager at the sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was bold and loved the fight; the sight of the enemy always stirred him.

sentences.zh: 德威老將，常務持重以挫人之鋒，故其用兵，常伺敵之隙以取勝。

translations.literal: Dewei was an old general and always aimed at steadiness to blunt the enemy’s edge; therefore in his use of troops he usually watched for the enemy’s gap to win.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei, the veteran, always played for weight and patience to dull the enemy’s edge; his battles turned on waiting for the other side’s mistake.

sentences.zh: 十五年，德威將燕兵三萬人，與鎮、定等軍從莊宗於河上，自麻家渡進軍臨濮，以趨汴州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Dewei led thirty thousand Yan troops, and with the armies of Zhen and Ding followed Zhuangzong on the river; from Majia Ford he advanced to Linpu, pressing toward Bian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Dewei led thirty thousand Yan troops with the hosts of Zhen and Ding behind Zhuangzong on the Yellow River. From Majia Ford they marched on Linpu, aiming at Bian.

sentences.zh: 軍宿胡柳陂，黎明，候騎報曰：「梁軍至矣！

translations.literal: The army encamped at Huliu; at dawn the scouts reported: “The Liang army has arrived!
translations.idiomatic: They camped at Huliu. At dawn scouts reported: “Liang is here!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗問戰於德威，德威對曰：「此去汴州，信宿而近，梁軍父母妻子皆在其中，而梁人家國系此一舉。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong asked Dewei about fighting; Dewei answered: “From here to Bian prefecture is barely two days’ march; Liang’s parents, wives, and children are all within it, and Liang’s house and state hang on this one throw.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong asked whether to fight. Dewei said: “Bian is two days away. Liang’s families and throne are inside that city. They must throw everything into this battle.

sentences.zh: 吾以深入之兵，當其必死之戰，可以計勝，而難與力爭也。

translations.literal: We with deeply committed troops face their fight to the death—we can win by plan, but it will be hard to match them in brute force.
translations.idiomatic: Our deep column meets their last stand. We can win by craft, not by shoving strength against strength.

sentences.zh: 且吾軍先至此，糧爨具而營柵完，是謂以逸待勞之師也。

translations.literal: Moreover our army reached here first; cooking gear is ready and the palisade complete—we are the rested army waiting on the weary.
translations.idiomatic: We arrived first. Fires are lit and the camp is set. We are the rested host waiting on the tired.

sentences.zh: 王宜按軍無動，而臣請以騎軍擾之，使其營柵不得成，樵爨不暇給，因其勞乏而乘之，可以勝也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should hold the army still, and let your servant use cavalry to harass them so their palisade cannot be finished and wood and cooking cannot keep pace; then strike when they are worn out and we can win.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the line, Majesty. Let me harry them with horse so their camp never sets and their wood and cook-fires fall behind—then strike when they break and we win.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗曰：「吾軍河上，終日俟敵，今見敵不擊，復何為乎？

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong said: “Our army has waited on the river all day for the enemy—now that we see them and do not strike, what else are we here for?
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong said: “We waited on this river all day for them. See the enemy and not strike—then why come at all?

sentences.zh: 」顧李存審曰：「公以輜重先，吾為公殿。

translations.literal: ” He turned to Li Cun’an and said: “You take the baggage train ahead—I will cover the rear for you.
translations.idiomatic: ” He turned to Li Cun’an: “Take the baggage first. I will cover your rear.

sentences.zh: 」遽督軍而出。

translations.literal: ” He hurriedly drove the army out.
translations.idiomatic: ” and drove the army out at once.

sentences.zh: 德威謂其子曰：「吾不知死所矣！

translations.literal: Dewei told his son: “I do not know where I will die!
translations.idiomatic: Dewei told his son: “I do not know where I will fall!

sentences.zh: 」前遇梁軍而陣：王居中，鎮、定之軍居左，德威之軍居右，而輜重次右之西。

translations.literal: They met the Liang army and drew up: the king was in the center, the armies of Zhen and Ding on the left, Dewei’s army on the right, and the baggage train behind the right wing to the west.
translations.idiomatic: They met Liang and formed: Zhuangzong in the center, Zhen and Ding on the left, Dewei on the right, baggage west of the right wing.

sentences.zh: 兵已接，莊宗率銀槍軍馳入梁陣，梁軍小敗，犯晉輜重，輜重見梁朱旗，皆驚走入德威軍，德威軍亂，梁軍乘之，德威父子皆戰死。

translations.literal: Once the lines engaged, Zhuangzong led the Silver Spear Army in a charge into the Liang formation; the Liang army suffered a small defeat, then struck Jin’s baggage train; the baggage train saw Liang’s vermilion banners and all fled in alarm into Dewei’s army; Dewei’s army fell into disorder; the Liang army pressed the advantage, and Dewei and his son both died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: As the lines met, Zhuangzong led the Silver Spear corps into Liang’s ranks. Liang buckled briefly, then hit Jin’s baggage. The train saw Liang’s red banners and panicked into Dewei’s wing. Dewei’s line collapsed. Liang pressed hard, and Dewei and his son both fell.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與諸將相持而哭曰：「吾不聽老將之言，而使其父子至此！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong stood facing the generals and wept: “I would not listen to the old general’s words, and so brought his father and son to this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong faced his commanders in tears: “I would not hear the old general—and now father and son are gone because of me!

sentences.zh: 」莊宗即位，贈德威太師。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Dewei as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he posthumously made Dewei Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，加贈太尉，配享莊宗廟。

translations.literal: In Mingzong’s time he was further enfeoffed as Grand Marshal and given paired sacrifice in Zhuangzong’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was further honored as Grand Marshal and given paired sacrifice in Zhuangzong’s temple.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖追封德威燕王。

translations.literal: Gaozu of Later Jin posthumously enfeoffed Dewei as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu of Later Jin posthumously made him Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 子光輔，官至刺史。

translations.literal: His son Guangfu reached the office of regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangfu rose to regional inspector.

sentences.zh: 符存審

translations.literal: Fu Cunshen
translations.idiomatic: Fu Cunshen

sentences.zh: （子彥超 彥饒 彥卿）〉

translations.literal: (with sons Yanchao, Yanrao, and Yanqing)〉
translations.idiomatic: (with sons Yanchao, Yanrao, and Yanqing)〉

sentences.zh: 符存審，字德詳，陳州宛丘人也。

translations.literal: Fu Cunshen, styled Dexiang, was a native of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Cunshen, styled Dexiang, came from Wanqiu in Chen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初名存，少微賤，嘗犯法當死，臨刑，指旁壞垣顧主者曰：「願就死於彼，冀得垣土覆屍。

translations.literal: His original name was Cun; in youth he was very lowly; he once broke the law and was condemned to death; at execution he pointed to a broken wall nearby and looked at the officer in charge, saying: “I wish to die there, hoping the wall’s earth may cover my corpse.
translations.idiomatic: He was first called Cun. Born poor, he once broke the law and was sentenced to die. At the block he pointed to a crumbling wall and begged the officer: “Let me die there, so the fallen earth may cover my body.

sentences.zh: 」主者哀而許之，為徙垣下。

translations.literal: ” The officer in charge took pity and agreed, and had him moved beneath the wall.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officer took pity and moved him under the wall.

sentences.zh: 而主將方飲酒，顧其愛妓，思得善歌者佐酒，妓言：「有符存常為妾歌，甚善。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the commandant was drinking wine and glanced at his favorite courtesan, wishing for a good singer to join the cup; the courtesan said: “There is one Fu Cun who often sang for me—he is very skilled.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant was drinking and wanted a good voice beside his cup. His favorite courtesan said: “Fu Cun used to sing for me—he sings well.

sentences.zh: 」主將馳騎召存審，而存審以徙垣下故，未加刑，因往就召，使歌而悅之，存審因得不死。

translations.literal: ” The commandant sent a rider at speed to summon Cunshen; because he had been moved beneath the wall he had not yet been executed; he therefore went to answer the summons, was made to sing, and pleased the commandant, and Cunshen thus escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: ” The commandant sent a rider in haste. Because Cunshen had been moved to the wall he had not yet been killed; he came when called, sang, and won the commandant’s favor—and lived.

sentences.zh: 其後事李罕之，從罕之歸晉，晉王以為義兒軍使，賜姓李氏，名存審。

translations.literal: Later he served Li Hanzhi; he followed Hanzhi in surrendering to Jin; the Prince of Jin made him commander of the foster-son corps, bestowed the surname Li, and named him Cunshen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Li Hanzhi and followed him over to Jin. The Prince of Jin made him commander of the foster-son corps, gave him the surname Li, and named him Cunshen.

sentences.zh: 從晉王擊李匡儔，為前鋒，破居庸關。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Jin in attacking Li Kuangchou, served as vanguard, and broke Juyong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Jin against Li Kuangchou as vanguard and broke Juyong Pass.

sentences.zh: 又從擊王行瑜，破龍泉寨，以功遷檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: He again followed in attacking Wang Xingyu, broke Longquan Stockade, and for merit was transferred to acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He marched again against Wang Xingyu, took Longquan Stockade, and was made acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 從李嗣昭攻汾州，執李瑭，遷左右廂步軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Li Sizhao in attacking Fen prefecture, captured Li Tang, and was transferred to commander of the left and right wing step armies.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Sizhao against Fen prefecture, took Li Tang, and was made commander of the left and right wing step armies.

sentences.zh: 又從嗣昭攻潞州，降丁會。

translations.literal: He again followed Sizhao in attacking Luzhou and induced Ding Hui to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sizhao again against Luzhou and brought Ding Hui over.

sentences.zh: 從周德威破梁夾城，遷忻州刺史、蕃漢馬步軍指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Zhou Dewei in breaking Liang’s twin fortifications, was transferred to prefect of Xin, and made commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhou Dewei in breaking Liang’s twin fortifications, became prefect of Xin, and was named commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 晉、趙攻燕，梁救燕，擊趙深州，圍蓚縣，存審與史建瑭軍下博，擊走梁軍，遷領邢州團練使。

translations.literal: Jin and Zhao attacked Yan; Liang came to Yan’s aid, struck Shenzhou in Zhao, and besieged Suo county. Cunshen and Shi Jiantang camped at Xiabo, drove off the Liang army, and Cunshen was transferred to serve as training commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and Zhao marched on Yan; Liang rode to Yan’s rescue, struck Shenzhou in Zhao, and laid siege to Suo county. Cunshen and Shi Jiantang took Xiabo, broke the Liang host, and Cunshen was made training commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏博叛梁降晉，存審為前鋒，屯臨清。

translations.literal: When Weibo rebelled against Liang and submitted to Jin, Cunshen served as vanguard and encamped at Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo turned on Liang and went over to Jin. Cunshen led the van and encamped at Linqing.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入魏，存審殿軍魏縣，與劉掞相距於莘西。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Wei, Cunshen brought up the rear at Wei county and faced Liu Yan west of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong entered Wei; Cunshen held the rear at Wei county and faced Liu Yan west of Shen.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗敗掞於故元城，閻寶以邢州降，乃以存審為安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Following Zhuangzong’s defeat of Liu Yan at former Yuancheng, Yan Bao surrendered Xingzhou, and Cunshen was appointed military governor of Anguo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong broke Liu Yan at former Yuancheng and Yan Bao surrendered Xingzhou, Cunshen was made military governor of Anguo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 毛璋以滄州降，徙存審橫海，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Mao Zhang surrendered Cangzhou; Cunshen was transferred to Henghai and made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhang gave up Cangzhou, and Cunshen was moved to Henghai and made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 契丹圍幽州，是時晉與梁相持河上，欲發兵，兵少，欲勿救，懼失之。

translations.literal: The Khitan besieged Youzhou. Jin and Liang were deadlocked on the river; the court wished to send troops but had too few, and feared to send none and lose the city.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan forces besieged Youzhou. Jin and Liang still faced each other across the river. The court wanted to send help but had too few men—and feared that if it sent none, Youzhou would be lost.

sentences.zh: 莊宗疑，以問諸將，而存審獨以為當救，曰：「願假臣騎兵五千足矣！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was uncertain and asked his generals; only Cunshen thought they should go, saying: “Give me five thousand cavalry and it will be enough!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong wavered and polled his generals. Only Cunshen argued they must go: “Give me five thousand horsemen—that is enough!

sentences.zh: 」乃遣存審分兵救之，卒擊走契丹。

translations.literal: ” So Cunshen was sent with a divided force to the rescue, and in the end drove off the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Cunshen was sent with a detachment, and in the end drove the Khitan off.

sentences.zh: 從戰胡柳陂，晉軍晨敗，亡周德威，存審與其子彥圖力戰，暮復敗梁軍於土山，遂取德勝，築河南北為兩城，晉人謂之「夾寨」。

translations.literal: He fought at Huliu Embankment. The Jin army was beaten in the morning and lost Zhou Dewei. Cunshen and his son Yan Tu fought hard; at dusk they again defeated the Liang army at Tushan, took Desheng, and built two cities north and south of the river—the Jin people called them the “Twin Forts.”
translations.idiomatic: At Huliu Embankment the Jin army was routed at dawn and Zhou Dewei fell. Cunshen and his son Yan Tu fought on; by evening they had broken the Liang force at Tushan, retaken Desheng, and raised twin cities north and south of the river—the Jin called them the “Pincer Forts.”

sentences.zh: 遷內外蕃漢馬步軍總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to overall commander of inner and outer barbarian and Han horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: He was made overall commander of the inner and outer barbarian and Han horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 梁朱友謙以河中同州降晉，梁遣劉掞攻同州，友謙求救，乃遣存審與李嗣昭救之。

translations.literal: Zhu Youqian of Liang surrendered Hezhong and Tongzhou to Jin. Liang sent Liu Yan to attack Tongzhou; Youqian called for aid, and Cunshen was sent with Li Sizhao to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian of Liang surrendered Hezhong and Tongzhou to Jin. Liang sent Liu Yan against Tongzhou; Youqian called for help, and Cunshen went with Li Sizhao to answer.

sentences.zh: 河中兵少而弱，梁人素易之，且不虞晉軍之速至也。

translations.literal: Hezhong’s troops were few and weak; the Liang men had always looked down on them and did not expect Jin forces to arrive so quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong’s army was small and weak. Liang had always despised it and never dreamed Jin would come so fast.

sentences.zh: 存審選精騎二百雜河中兵出擊掞壘，陽敗而走，掞兵追之，晉騎反擊，獲其騎兵五十，梁人知其晉軍也，皆大驚。

translations.literal: Cunshen chose two hundred crack horsemen, mixed them with Hezhong troops, and struck Liu Yan’s camp. They feigned defeat and fled; Yan’s men pursued, and the Jin cavalry wheeled and counterattacked, taking fifty of his horsemen. The Liang men knew Jin had come and were all greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen picked two hundred elite riders, mingled them with Hezhong troops, and hit Liu Yan’s camp. They played at defeat and ran; Yan’s men chased, and the Jin horsemen turned and cut them down, taking fifty riders. Once Liang knew Jin had arrived, panic spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 然河中糧少而新降，人心頗持兩端，晉軍屯朝邑，諸將皆欲速戰，存審曰：「使梁軍知吾利於速戰，則將夾渭而營，斷我餉道，以持久困我，則進退不可，敗之道也。

translations.literal: Yet Hezhong had little grain and had only just submitted; hearts were divided. The Jin army encamped at Chaoyi, and the generals all wanted a quick fight. Cunshen said: “If Liang learns we favor speed, they will camp on both banks of the Wei, cut our supply line, and wear us down in a long stand—then advance and retreat alike become impossible. That is the road to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong’s granaries were thin and the city had only just turned; loyalties still wavered. Jin encamped at Chaoyi, and every general wanted battle at once. Cunshen said: “Let Liang see we want a quick fight and they will fortify both banks of the Wei, sever our supplies, and grind us down. Then we cannot advance or retreat. That is how armies die.

sentences.zh: 不若緩師示弱，伺隙出奇，可以取勝。

translations.literal: Better to slacken the march, show weakness, watch for an opening, and strike with surprise—then victory can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Better to slow the march, look weak, wait for a gap, and strike from nowhere. That is how victory is won.

sentences.zh: 」乃按軍不動。

translations.literal: ” So he held the army still.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kept the army in place.

sentences.zh: 居旬日，望氣者言：「有黑氣，狀如鬥雞。

translations.literal: After ten days a diviner of vapors said: “There is black vapor shaped like fighting cocks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days passed. A reader of vapors said: “Black vapor rises, shaped like fighting cocks.

sentences.zh: 」存審曰：「可以一戰矣！

translations.literal: ” Cunshen said: “We can fight now!
translations.idiomatic: ” Cunshen said: “The moment has come!

sentences.zh: 」乃進軍擊掞，大敗之，掞閉壁不復出。

translations.literal: ” He advanced and struck Liu Yan, defeating him greatly; Yan shut himself behind his walls and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: ” He marched forward and smashed Liu Yan. Yan sealed himself in his walls and would not come out again.

sentences.zh: 存審曰：「掞兵已敗，不如逸之。

translations.literal: Cunshen said: “Yan’s army is already beaten—better to let him escape.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen said: “Yan is already broken. Better to let him slip away.

sentences.zh: 」乃休士卒，遣裨將王建及牧馬於沙苑，掞以謂晉軍且懈，乃夜遁去，存審追擊於渭河，又大敗之。

translations.literal: ” He rested the troops and sent the deputy Wang Jianji to graze horses at Shayuan. Yan thought the Jin army was slackening and fled by night; Cunshen pursued to the Wei River and again defeated him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rested the men and sent the deputy Wang Jianji to graze horses at Shayuan. Yan took it for slackness and bolted by night. Cunshen chased him to the Wei River and broke him again.

sentences.zh: 張文禮弒趙王王镕，晉遣閻寶、李嗣昭等攻之，至輒戰死，最後遣存審破之。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Zhao king Wang Rong. Jin sent Yan Bao, Li Sizhao, and others against him; they died in battle one after another, until at last Cunshen was sent and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli murdered the Zhao king Wang Rong. Jin sent Yan Bao, Li Sizhao, and others against him; one after another they fell in battle, until Cunshen was sent and broke him at last.

sentences.zh: 存審為將有機略，大小百餘戰，未嘗敗衄，與周德威齊名。

translations.literal: As a commander Cunshen had tactical cunning; in more than a hundred battles large and small he never suffered defeat, and his name stood equal to Zhou Dewei’s.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen commanded with cunning. In more than a hundred fights, great and small, he never tasted defeat—and his name stood beside Zhou Dewei’s.

sentences.zh: 德威死，晉之舊將獨存審在。

translations.literal: When Dewei died, of Jin’s old generals only Cunshen remained.
translations.idiomatic: When Dewei fell, of Jin’s old commanders only Cunshen was left.

sentences.zh: 契丹攻遮虜，乃以存審為盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: The Khitan attacked Zhelu, and Cunshen was made military governor of Lulong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan forces struck Zhelu, and Cunshen was made military governor of Lulong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時存審已病，辭不肯行，莊宗使人慰諭，強遣之。

translations.literal: By then Cunshen was already ill; he declined and refused to go. Zhuangzong sent men to comfort and instruct him and forced him to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen was already sick. He begged off and would not go. Zhuangzong sent envoys to coax him—and then compelled him to leave.

sentences.zh: 莊宗滅梁入洛，存審自以身為大將，不得與破梁之功，怏怏，疾益甚，因請朝京師。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Luoyang, Cunshen brooded that as a great general he had not shared in the final victory over Liang. Discontented, he grew worse in illness and asked to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and entered Luoyang, Cunshen brooded that a great general ought to have stood in the final victory—and he had not. His discontent fed his illness, and he asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 是時，郭崇韜權位已重，然其名望素出存審下，不樂其來而加己上，因沮其事，存審妻郭氏泣訴於崇韜曰：「吾夫於國有功，而於公鄉里之舊，奈何忍令死棄窮野！

translations.literal: By then Guo Chongtao’s power and rank were already heavy, yet his renown had always stood below Cunshen’s; he did not relish Cunshen’s coming to rank above him and blocked the request. Cunshen’s wife, Lady Guo, wept before Chongtao and pleaded: “My husband has served the state with merit, and you are old neighbors from the same district—how can you bear to let him die abandoned in the wild!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao’s power was already immense, yet his fame had never matched Cunshen’s. He did not want Cunshen to arrive and stand above him, and he blocked the request. Cunshen’s wife Lady Guo wept before Chongtao: “My husband served the state with merit, and you are old neighbors from the same home—how can you leave him to die in the wilderness!

sentences.zh: 」崇韜愈怒。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao grew only angrier.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 存審章累上，輒不許，存審伏枕嘆曰：「老夫事二主四十年，今日天下一家，四夷遠俗，至於亡國之將、射鉤斬袪之人，皆得親見天子，奉觴為壽，而獨予棄死於此，豈非命哉！

translations.literal: Cunshen’s memorials piled up and were always denied. From his sickbed he sighed: “I served two sovereigns for forty years. Today the realm is one house; even defeated enemy generals and men who had wounded their lords with bow or blade are allowed to see the Son of Heaven and raise a cup for his long life—yet I alone am left to die here. Is this not fate!
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen’s memorials piled up and were always refused. From his sickbed he sighed: “Forty years I served two masters. Now the realm is one; even ruined enemy generals and men who once drew bow or blade against their lords are allowed to see the Son of Heaven and drink to his long life—and I alone am left to die here. Is this not fate!

sentences.zh: 」崇韜度存審病已亟，乃請許其來朝。

translations.literal: ” Chongtao, judging that Cunshen’s illness was already grave, then asked that he be allowed to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chongtao, seeing that Cunshen was near death, at last asked that he be allowed to come to court.

sentences.zh: 徙存審宣武軍節度使，卒於幽州。

translations.literal: Cunshen was transferred to military governor of Xuanwu Army and died at Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen was transferred to military governor of Xuanwu Army and died at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨終，戒其子曰：「吾少提一劍去鄉里，四十年間取將相，然履鋒冒刃出死入生而得至此也。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he warned his sons: “I left home with a single sword; in forty years I rose to general and councilor—but I reached this place only by treading blades and passing through death again and again.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his sons: “I left home with one sword. In forty years I rose to general and councilor—but I got here only by walking through blades, out of death and back into life again and again.

sentences.zh: 」因出其平生身所中矢鏃百餘而示之曰：「爾其勉哉！」

translations.literal: ” He then brought out more than a hundred arrowheads lodged in his body across his life and showed them, saying: “Do your utmost!
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he brought out more than a hundred arrowheads taken from his body over a lifetime and showed them. “Now do your utmost,” he said.

sentences.zh: 存審三子：彥超、彥饒、彥卿。

translations.literal: Cunshen had three sons: Yan Chao, Yan Rao, and Yan Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen had three sons: Yan Chao, Yan Rao, and Yan Qing.

sentences.zh: 彥超為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Yan Chao was prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chao served as prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 郭從謙弒莊宗，明宗入洛陽，是時，彥超為北京巡檢，永王存霸奔於太原，彥超見留守張憲謀之。

translations.literal: When Guo Congqian murdered Zhuangzong and Mingzong entered Luoyang, Yan Chao was northern-capital inspector. Prince of Yong Cunba fled toward Taiyuan, and Yan Chao met acting governor Zhang Xian to plot with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Congqian murdered Zhuangzong and Mingzong entered Luoyang, Yan Chao was northern-capital inspector. Prince of Yong Cunba fled toward Taiyuan, and Yan Chao met Taiyuan’s acting governor Zhang Xian to plan with him.

sentences.zh: 憲，儒者，事莊宗最久，不忍背恩，欲納之，彥超不從，存霸遂見殺。

translations.literal: Zhang, a scholar, had served Zhuangzong longest and could not bear to betray that debt; he wished to harbor Cunba, but Yan Chao would not agree, and Cunba was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was a man of letters who had served Zhuangzong longest and could not betray that debt. He wanted to shelter Cunba; Yan Chao refused—and Cunba was killed.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，彥超來朝，明宗德之，勞曰：「河東無事，賴爾之力也。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Yan Chao came to court. Mingzong honored him and said in consolation: “The eastern capital stayed quiet—your strength did that.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong took the throne Yan Chao came to court. Mingzong praised him: “The eastern capital stayed calm—we owe that to you.

sentences.zh: 」以為建雄軍留後。

translations.literal: ” He was made acting governor of Jianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was made acting governor of Jianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 遷北京留守，徙鎮昭義，罷為上將軍，復為泰寧軍節度使，又徙安遠。

translations.literal: He was transferred to northern-capital governor, then to Zhaoyi, dismissed to senior general, restored as military governor of Taining Army, and again transferred to Anyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He became northern-capital governor, then Zhaoyi governor, was dismissed to senior general, returned as military governor of Taining Army, and was transferred again to Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 彥超主藏奴王希全盜其貲，彥超稍責之，奴懼，夜叩其門，言有急，彥超出，見殺，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Yan Chao’s chief storehouse slave Wang Xiquan stole his goods. Yan Chao rebuked him slightly; the slave grew afraid, knocked at his gate at night claiming urgent business, and killed Yan Chao when he came out. He was posthumously made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Chao’s chief storehouse slave Wang Xiquan stole from him. Yan Chao scolded him lightly; the slave panicked, knocked at his gate at night crying emergency, and killed him when he came out. Yan Chao was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 次子彥饒，為汴州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: The second son, Yan Rao, was commander of Bianzhou’s horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Yan Rao commanded Bianzhou’s horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，發汴兵三千戍瓦橋關，控鶴指揮使張諫為亂，殺權知州高逖，迫彥饒為帥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng three thousand Bian troops were sent to garrison Waqiao Pass. Konghe commander Zhang Jian mutinied, killed acting prefect Gao Di, and forced Yan Rao to become their leader.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year one three thousand Bian troops were sent to garrison Waqiao Pass. Konghe commander Zhang Jian mutinied, killed acting prefect Gao Di, and forced Yan Rao to lead them.

sentences.zh: 彥饒陽許之曰：「欲吾為帥，當止焚掠，明日以軍禮見吾於南衙。

translations.literal: Yan Rao outwardly agreed, saying: “If you want me as commander, stop the burning and looting. Tomorrow meet me with military ceremony at the southern yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rao agreed in public: “If you want me as commander, stop the burning and looting. Tomorrow meet me with full military ceremony at the southern yamen.

sentences.zh: 」乃陰與拱衙指揮使龐起伏甲於衙內。

translations.literal: ” In secret he arranged with Gongya commander Pang Yun to hide armed men inside the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: ” In secret he arranged with Gongya commander Pang Yun to hide armed men inside the yamen.

sentences.zh: 明日，諫等皆集，伏兵發，誅諫等，殺四百餘人，即日牒州事與推官韋儼。

translations.literal: The next day Jian and the others all assembled; the hidden troops sprang up, executed Jian and the rest, killed more than four hundred men, and that same day handed prefectural affairs to judicial officer Wei Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jian and the others gathered. The hidden troops rose, executed Jian and his men, killed more than four hundred, and that same day Yan Rao turned prefectural affairs over to judicial officer Wei Yan.

sentences.zh: 明宗下詔褒其忠略。

translations.literal: Mingzong issued an edict praising his loyalty and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong issued an edict praising his loyalty and cunning.

sentences.zh: 其後累遷彰聖都指揮使，歷曹、沂、饒三州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he rose through successive posts to Zhangsheng Army commander and served as prefect of Cao, Yi, and Rao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose to Zhangsheng Army commander and served as prefect of Cao, Yi, and Rao in turn.

sentences.zh: 清泰三年，自饒州刺史拜忠正軍節度使、侍衛馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingtai he was promoted from Rao prefect to military governor of Zhongzheng Army and commander of the palace horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai year three he rose from Rao prefect to military governor of Zhongzheng Army and commander of the palace horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖起太原，彥饒以侍衛兵從廢帝至河陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu of Jin rose at Taiyuan, Yan Rao led the palace guard following the deposed emperor to Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin rose at Taiyuan, Yan Rao led the palace guard with the deposed emperor to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 廢帝敗，晉高祖以楊光遠代彥饒將親軍，徙彥饒義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor was defeated, Gaozu replaced Yan Rao’s command of the personal army with Yang Guangyuan and transferred Yan Rao to military governor of Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor fell, Gaozu put Yang Guangyuan in command of the personal army in Yan Rao’s place and transferred Yan Rao to Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 範延光反，白奉進以侍衛兵三千屯滑州。

translations.literal: When Fan Yanguang rebelled, Bai Fengjin stationed three thousand palace troops at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang rebelled, Bai Fengjin encamped three thousand palace troops at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 兵士犯法，奉進捕得五人，其三人義成兵也，因並斬之，彥饒怒。

translations.literal: Soldiers broke the law; Fengjin captured five of them, three of whom were Yicheng troops, and executed all five together. Yan Rao was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers broke the law. Fengjin caught five of them—three from Yicheng’s ranks—and beheaded all five together. Yan Rao was furious.

sentences.zh: 明日，奉進從數騎過彥饒謝不先告而殺，彥饒曰：「軍士各有部分，義成兵卒豈公所得斬邪？

translations.literal: The next day Fengjin came with a few riders to apologize for killing without prior notice. Yan Rao said: “Soldiers each belong to their own command—how could you execute Yicheng troops?
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fengjin came with a few riders to apologize for killing without warning. Yan Rao said: “Every soldier belongs to his own command—how dare you behead Yicheng men?

sentences.zh: 何無主客之禮也！

translations.literal: Where is the courtesy due between host and guest!
translations.idiomatic: Where is the courtesy owed between host and guest!

sentences.zh: 」奉進怒曰：「軍士犯法，安有彼此！

translations.literal: ” Fengjin raged: “When soldiers break the law, what difference between one and another!
translations.idiomatic: ” Fengjin snapped: “When soldiers break the law, what difference does it make whose they are!

sentences.zh: 且仆已自謝過，而公怒不息，欲與延光同反邪！

translations.literal: And I have already apologized—yet your anger will not cease. Do you mean to rebel with Yanguang!
translations.idiomatic: I have already apologized, and still your anger will not die. Do you mean to rebel with Yanguang!

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而起，彥饒不復留之，其麾下大噪，追奉進殺之，彥饒不之止也。

translations.literal: ” He swept his robes and rose. Yan Rao did not detain him; his troops raised a great clamor, pursued Fengjin, and killed him—and Yan Rao did not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: ” He flung his robes aside and stalked out. Yan Rao made no move to hold him back. His troops erupted, chased Fengjin down, and killed him—and Yan Rao did not stop them.

sentences.zh: 已而屯駐軍將馬萬等聞亂，以兵擒彥饒送之京師，遂以彥饒應延光反聞。

translations.literal: Soon after, the garrison commanders Ma Wan and others heard of the turmoil, seized Yan Rao with troops, and sent him to the capital. He was then reported as having joined Yanguang’s rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the garrison commanders Ma Wan and others heard of the uproar, seized Yan Rao with troops, and sent him to the capital. Word went out that he had joined Yanguang’s rebellion.

sentences.zh: 行至赤岡，高祖使人殺之，下詔削奪在身官爵。

translations.literal: At Chigang Gaozu had him killed and issued an edict stripping his titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At Chigang Gaozu had him executed and stripped him of every title and rank.

sentences.zh: 彥饒與晉初無釁隙，以一旦之忿，不能馭其軍，殺奉進已非其本意，以反見誅，非其罪也！

translations.literal: Yan Rao had no prior grievance with Jin. In a moment of rage he failed to control his army; killing Fengjin was never his intent, yet he was condemned as a rebel and put to death for a crime that was not truly his!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rao had no old quarrel with Jin. In a flash of anger he lost control of his men; killing Fengjin was never what he meant—and yet he died condemned as a rebel, punished for a crime that was not truly his!

sentences.zh: 史建瑭

translations.literal: Shi Jiantang
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jiantang

sentences.zh: （子匡翰）〉

translations.literal: (son Kuang Han)〉
translations.idiomatic: (son Kuang Han)〉

sentences.zh: 史建瑭，雁門人也。

translations.literal: Shi Jiantang was a native of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jiantang came from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 晉王為雁門節度使，其父敬思為九府都督，從晉王入關破黃巢，復京師，擊秦宗權於陳州，嘗將騎兵為先鋒。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin was military governor of Yanmen, Jiantang’s father Jingsi served as commander of the nine garrisons. He followed the Prince of Jin through the pass to break Huang Chao, recover the capital, and strike Qin Zongquan at Chenzhou, often leading cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin governed Yanmen, Jiantang’s father Jingsi commanded the nine garrisons. He followed the prince through the pass to break Huang Chao, recover the capital, and strike Qin Zongquan at Chenzhou, often leading the cavalry van.

sentences.zh: 晉王東追黃巢於冤朐，還過梁，軍其城北。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin pursued Huang Chao east to Yuanqu and, returning past Liang, camped north of their city.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin pursued Huang Chao east to Yuanqu and, on the return, passed Liang and camped north of the city.

sentences.zh: 梁王置酒上源驛，獨敬思與薛鐵山、賀回鶻等十餘人侍。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler held wine at Shangyuan post station; only Jingsi, Xue Tieshan, He Huihu, and a dozen others attended.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler held wine at Shangyuan post station. Only Jingsi, Xue Tieshan, He Huihu, and a dozen others waited on him.

sentences.zh: 晉王醉，留宿梁驛，梁兵夜圍而攻之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin drank heavily and stayed overnight at the Liang station; Liang troops surrounded and attacked by night.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin drank deep and stayed the night at the Liang station. Liang troops surrounded it and attacked after dark.

sentences.zh: 敬思登驛樓，射殺梁兵十餘人，會天大雨，晉王得與從者俱去，縋尉氏門以出。

translations.literal: Jingsi climbed the station tower and shot down more than ten Liang soldiers. Heavy rain fell; the Prince of Jin escaped with his followers and lowered themselves from Weishi Gate to get out.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsi climbed the station tower and shot down more than ten Liang soldiers. Rain poured down; the prince and his followers escaped by lowering themselves from Weishi Gate.

sentences.zh: 而敬思為梁追兵所得，見殺。

translations.literal: But Jingsi was taken by Liang pursuers and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsi was caught by Liang pursuers and killed.

sentences.zh: 建瑭少事軍中為裨校，自晉降丁會，與梁相距於潞州，建瑭已為晉兵先鋒。

translations.literal: Jiantang entered service young as a junior officer in the army. After Jin submitted to Ding Hui they faced Liang at Luzhou; Jiantang was already serving as Jin vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantang entered the army young as a junior officer. After Jin submitted to Ding Hui and faced Liang at Luzhou, Jiantang already led the Jin van.

sentences.zh: 梁兵數為建瑭所殺，相戒常避史先鋒。

translations.literal: Liang troops fell again and again to Jiantang; they warned one another to keep clear of Shi’s vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang soldiers kept dying to Jiantang. They warned one another: steer clear of Shi’s vanguard.

sentences.zh: 梁遣王景仁攻趙，晉軍救趙，建瑭以先鋒兵出井陘，戰於柏鄉。

translations.literal: Liang sent Wang Jingren against Zhao; Jin rode to the rescue, and Jiantang led vanguard forces out through Jingxing to fight at Baixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Wang Jingren against Zhao. Jin marched to the rescue, and Jiantang led the van through Jingxing to fight at Baixiang.

sentences.zh: 梁軍為方陣，分其兵為二：汴、宋之軍居左，魏、滑之軍居右。

translations.literal: The Liang army formed square battalions and split its force in two: Bian and Song on the left, Wei and Hua on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang army drew up in square battalions and split its force: Bian and Song on the left, Wei and Hua on the right.

sentences.zh: 周德威擊其左，建瑭擊其右，梁軍皆走，遂大敗之。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei struck the left; Jiantang struck the right. The Liang armies all fled, and they were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei smashed the left; Jiantang broke the right. The Liang lines broke and ran, and the army was ruined.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: For this he was made Acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made Acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 天祐九年，晉攻燕，燕王劉守光乞師於梁，梁太祖自將擊趙，圍棗強、蓚縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianyou Jin attacked Yan. Yan king Liu Shouguang begged Liang for troops; Liang Taizu personally led an attack on Zhao and besieged Zaoqiang and Suo county.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year nine Jin attacked Yan. Yan king Liu Shouguang begged Liang for aid; Liang Taizu himself marched against Zhao and besieged Zaoqiang and Suo county.

sentences.zh: 是時晉精兵皆北攻燕，獨符存審與建瑭以三千騎屯趙州。

translations.literal: Jin’s crack troops were all north attacking Yan; only Fu Cunshen and Jiantang held Zhaozhou with three thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: All Jin’s best troops were north against Yan. Only Fu Cunshen and Jiantang held Zhaozhou with three thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 梁軍已破棗強，存審扼下博橋。

translations.literal: Liang had already broken Zaoqiang; Cunshen held Xiabo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had already taken Zaoqiang. Cunshen held Xiabo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 建瑭分其麾下五百騎為五隊：一之衡水，一之南宮，一之信都，一之阜城，而自將其一，約各取梁芻牧者十人會下博。

translations.literal: Jiantang split five hundred of his men into five squads: one to Hengshui, one to Nangong, one to Xindu, one to Fucheng, and he led the fifth himself. Each was to seize ten Liang foragers and meet at Xiabo.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantang split five hundred men into five squads—one to Hengshui, one to Nangong, one to Xindu, one to Fucheng, and he led the fifth. Each squad was to seize ten Liang foragers and rendezvous at Xiabo.

sentences.zh: 至暮，擒梁兵數十，皆殺之，各留其一人，縱使逸去，告之曰：「晉王軍且大至。

translations.literal: By evening they had captured dozens of Liang soldiers, killed them all, and kept one from each group alive. They released them and said: “The Prince of Jin’s army will arrive in force.
translations.idiomatic: By evening they had taken dozens of Liang soldiers, killed all but one from each squad, and let the survivors go with word that the Prince of Jin’s army was coming in force.

sentences.zh: 」明日，建瑭率百騎為梁旗幟，雜其芻牧者，暮叩梁營，殺其守門卒，縱火大呼，斬擊數十百人。

translations.literal: ” The next day Jiantang led a hundred horsemen under Liang banners, mixed with the captured foragers, and at dusk struck the Liang camp. They killed the gate guards, set fires and shouted, and cut down scores of men.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next day Jiantang rode at the head of a hundred horsemen under Liang banners, mingled with the captured foragers, and at dusk hit the Liang camp. They killed the gate guards, set fires, shouted, and cut down scores of men.

sentences.zh: 而梁芻牧者所出，各遇晉兵，有所亡失，其縱而不殺者，歸而皆言晉軍且至。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the foraging parties Jiantang had sent out each met Jin troops and suffered losses; those he had spared to escape returned and all said Jin forces were coming.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the foragers Jiantang had sent out each ran into Jin troops and lost men. Those he had spared to escape came back saying Jin was near.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖夜拔營去，蓚縣人追擊之，梁軍棄其輜重鎧甲不可勝計。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu broke camp and fled by night. People of Suo county pursued them; the Liang army abandoned baggage, armor, and equipment beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Taizu broke camp and fled by night. Suo county people chased them; Liang left baggage, armor, and gear beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖方病，由是增劇，而晉軍以故得並力以收燕者，二人之力也。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu was already ill; from this his condition worsened. Jin owed its united strength to take Yan largely to these two men’s efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Taizu was already sick, and from this he grew worse. Jin’s eventual united push to take Yan owed much to these two men.

sentences.zh: 後從莊宗入魏博，敗劉掞於故元城，累以功歷貝、相二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Jiantang followed Zhuangzong into Weibo and helped defeat Liu Yan at former Yuancheng, rising through successive appointments as prefect of Bei and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiantang followed Zhuangzong into Weibo, helped break Liu Yan at former Yuancheng, and rose through successive posts as prefect of Bei and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十八年，晉軍討張文禮於鎮州，建瑭以先鋒兵下趙州，執其刺史王珽。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Jin campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou. Jiantang led the vanguard down to Zhaozhou and seized its prefect Wang Ting.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen Jin campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou. Jiantang led the van to Zhaozhou and seized its prefect Wang Ting.

sentences.zh: 兵傅鎮州，建瑭攻其城門，中流矢卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: When the army closed on Zhenzhou Jiantang attacked the city gate, was struck by a flying arrow, and died at forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: When the army pressed Zhenzhou Jiantang assaulted the gate, took an arrow, and died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 子匡翰

translations.literal: Son Kuang Han
translations.idiomatic: Son Kuang Han

sentences.zh: 建瑭子匡翰，尚晉高祖女，是為魯國長公主。

translations.literal: Jiantang’s son Kuang Han married a daughter of Gaozu of Jin and became Princess of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantang’s son Kuang Han married a daughter of Gaozu of Jin and became Princess of Lu.

sentences.zh: 匡翰為將，沈毅有謀，而接下以禮，與部曲語未嘗不名。

translations.literal: As a commander Kuang Han was steady and resourceful; he treated subordinates with courtesy and never addressed his officers without using their names.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Han commanded with steady cunning. He treated subordinates with courtesy and never spoke to an officer without naming him.

sentences.zh: 歷天雄軍步軍都指揮使、彰聖馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He served as infantry commander of Tianxiong Army and cavalry commander of Zhangsheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as infantry commander of Tianxiong Army and cavalry commander of Zhangsheng Army.

sentences.zh: 事晉為懷和二州刺史、鄭州防禦使、義成軍節度使，所至兵民稱慕之。

translations.literal: Under Jin he held the prefectures of Huaihe and Er, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, and military governor of Yicheng Circuit; wherever he went soldiers and civilians admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he governed Huaihe and Er, served as defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and military governor of Yicheng Circuit—and wherever he went soldiers and people admired him.

sentences.zh: 史氏世為將，而匡翰好讀書，尤喜《春秋三傳》，與學者講論，終日無倦。

translations.literal: The Shi clan had been generals for generations, yet Kuang Han loved reading and especially favored the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, discussing them with scholars tirelessly through entire days.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi clan had bred generals for generations, yet Kuang Han loved books and above all the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, debating them with scholars all day without tiring.

sentences.zh: 義成軍從事關澈尤嗜酒，嘗醉罵匡翰曰：「近聞張彥澤臠張式，未見史匡翰斬關澈，天下談者未有偶爾！

translations.literal: Yicheng Circuit aide Guan Che was especially fond of wine. Once, drunk, he cursed Kuang Han: “Men lately speak of Zhang Yanzhe dismembering Zhang Shi—yet none have seen Shi Kuang Han behead Guan Che. Among those who talk, there is no pair!
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng Circuit aide Guan Che loved wine. Once, drunk, he cursed Kuang Han: “People talk of Zhang Yanzhe carving up Zhang Shi—but no one has yet seen Shi Kuang Han behead Guan Che. The gossips have no match for that!

sentences.zh: 」匡翰不怒，引滿自罰而慰勉之，人皆服其量。

translations.literal: ” Kuang Han was not angry; he filled his cup to penalize himself and offered comfort and encouragement. All admired his forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: ” Kuang Han did not rage. He filled his own cup in self-penalty, comforted Che, and urged him on. Everyone marveled at his measure.

sentences.zh: 卒年四十。

translations.literal: He died at forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty.

sentences.zh: 王建及

translations.literal: Wang Jianji
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianji

sentences.zh: 王建及，許州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jianji was a native of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianji came from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少事李罕之，從罕之奔晉，為匡衛指揮使。

translations.literal: In youth he served Li Hanzhi; following Hanzhi when he fled to Jin, he became drill commissioner of Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served Li Hanzhi. When Hanzhi fled to Jin, Jianji went with him and became drill commissioner of Kuangwei.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉戰柏鄉，相距鄗邑野河上，鎮、定兵扼河橋，梁兵急擊之。

translations.literal: When Liang and Jin fought at Baixiang, facing each other across the Ye River at Hao, Zhengding and Dingzhou troops held the river bridge while Liang forces attacked urgently.
translations.idiomatic: At Baixiang, Liang and Jin faced off across the Ye River at Hao. Zhengding and Dingzhou troops held the bridge while Liang hurled itself at them.

sentences.zh: 莊宗登高臺望見鎮、定兵將敗，顧建及曰：「橋為梁奪，則吾軍危矣，奈何？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong climbed a high platform, saw the Zhengding and Dingzhou troops about to lose, turned to Jianji and said: “If Liang takes the bridge, our army is in peril—what can we do?
translations.idiomatic: From a high platform Zhuangzong watched the Zhengding and Dingzhou lines buckle and turned to Jianji: “If Liang takes that bridge, we are finished—what do we do?

sentences.zh: 」建及選二百人馳擊梁兵，梁兵敗，解去。

translations.literal: ” Jianji selected two hundred men and charged the Liang army. Liang was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jianji picked two hundred men, galloped into the Liang ranks, broke them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 從戰莘縣、故元城，皆先登陷陣，以功累拜遼州刺史，將銀槍效節軍。

translations.literal: In battles at Shen county and Guyuan city he always led the assault first; for merit he was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Liaozhou, commanding the Silver Spear Valiant Loyalty Army.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen county and Guyuan city he was always first over the wall. Merit piled up until he was made prefect of Liaozhou and given the Silver Spear Valiant Loyalty Army.

sentences.zh: 晉攻楊劉，建及躬自負葭葦堙塹，先登拔之。

translations.literal: When Jin attacked Yangliu, Jianji himself carried reeds to fill the moat, led the assault, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin assaulted Yangliu, Jianji shouldered bundles of reeds himself to fill the ditch, climbed first, and took the place.

sentences.zh: 從戰胡柳，晉兵已敗，與梁爭土山，梁兵先至，登山而陣。

translations.literal: At Huliu, Jin had already been defeated; both sides fought for a hill. Liang arrived first, climbed and formed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At Huliu the Jin line had already broken. Both armies fought for a hill. Liang got there first, climbed it, and formed up.

sentences.zh: 莊宗至山下望梁陣堅而整，呼其軍曰：「今日之戰，得山者勝。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong reached the foot of the hill, saw Liang’s formation solid and orderly, and called to his army: “Today’s battle—who holds the hill wins.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong reached the foot of the hill, looked up at Liang’s tight ranks, and shouted to his men: “Whoever holds that hill wins today.

sentences.zh: 」因馳騎犯之，建及以銀槍軍繼進，梁兵下走，陣山西，晉兵遂得土山。

translations.literal: ” He charged in on horseback; Jianji followed with the Silver Spear Army. Liang troops fled down the hill to the west of the formation; Jin took the hill.
translations.idiomatic: ” He spurred forward. Jianji came behind with the Silver Spear Army. Liang broke and ran down the western slope; Jin seized the hill.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆言：「潰兵未集，日暮不可戰。

translations.literal: The generals all said: “The scattered troops have not reassembled; at dusk we cannot fight.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said: “Our broken units are not yet gathered. At dusk we cannot fight.

sentences.zh: 」閻寶曰：「彼陣山上，吾在其下，尚能擊之，況以高而擊下，不可失也。

translations.literal: ” Yan Bao said: “They hold the hill and we are below, yet we could still strike them—how much more if we attack from high ground down. We must not miss this.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan Bao said: “They stand on the height and we below, yet we still broke them once. Strike downhill and we cannot miss.

sentences.zh: 」建及以為然，因白莊宗曰：「請登高望臣破敵！

translations.literal: ” Jianji agreed and told Zhuangzong: “Please climb high and watch me break the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: ” Jianji agreed and told Zhuangzong: “Climb up and watch me smash them!

sentences.zh: 」即呼眾曰：「今日所失輜重皆在山西，盍往取之！

translations.literal: ” He then called to the troops: “Today’s lost baggage train is all west of the hill—shall we not go take it!
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he shouted to the ranks: “Everything we lost today sits west of the hill—why not go get it back!

sentences.zh: 」即馳犯梁陣，梁兵大敗。

translations.literal: ” He charged the Liang formation at once; Liang was routed.
translations.idiomatic: ” He charged straight into the Liang line. Liang collapsed.

sentences.zh: 晉遂軍德勝，為南北城於河上。

translations.literal: Jin then encamped at Desheng, building north and south cities on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then made camp at Desheng and raised north and south cities on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 梁將賀瑰攻其南城，以竹笮維戰艦於河，晉兵不得渡，南城危甚。

translations.literal: Liang general He Gui attacked the south city, linking warships on the river with bamboo chains. Jin could not cross; the south city was in grave danger.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s He Gui struck the south city, chaining his warships across the river with bamboo cables. Jin could not cross, and the south city hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 莊宗積金帛於軍門，募能破梁戰艦者，至於吐火禁咒莫不皆有。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong piled gold and silk at the army gate, recruiting anyone who could break Liang’s warships—from fire-breathing tricks to forbidden curses, every sort was tried.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong heaped gold and silk at the camp gate and offered reward to anyone who could break Liang’s fleet—fire-breathers, spell-charmers, every trick under heaven.

sentences.zh: 建及重鎧執槊呼曰：「梁、晉一水間爾，何必巧為！

translations.literal: Jianji in heavy armor grasped his spear and shouted: “Liang and Jin are separated by one stretch of water—why bother with tricks!
translations.idiomatic: Jianji in heavy mail gripped his spear and roared: “Liang and Jin are only one river apart—what need for tricks!

sentences.zh: 吾今破之矣。

translations.literal: I will break them now.
translations.idiomatic: I will break them now.

sentences.zh: 」即以大甕積薪，自上流縱火焚梁戰艦，建及以二舟載甲士隨之，斧其竹笮，梁兵皆走。

translations.literal: ” He piled firewood in great jars, floated them downstream with fire to burn Liang’s warships; Jianji followed in two boats carrying armored men, hacked through the bamboo chains, and Liang troops all fled.
translations.idiomatic: ” He loaded great jars with kindling, set them ablaze upstream, and sent them drifting into Liang’s ships. Two boats of armored men followed Jianji; they chopped through the bamboo chains and Liang fled.

sentences.zh: 晉軍乃得渡。

translations.literal: The Jin army was then able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could the Jin army cross.

sentences.zh: 救南城，瑰圍解去。

translations.literal: The south city was saved; Gui lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The south city was saved. Gui broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自莊宗得魏博，建及將銀槍效節軍。

translations.literal: From when Zhuangzong took Weibo, Jianji commanded the Silver Spear Valiant Loyalty Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong won Weibo, Jianji led the Silver Spear Valiant Loyalty Army.

sentences.zh: 建及為將，喜以家貲散士卒。

translations.literal: As a commander, Jianji loved to distribute his family wealth among his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander Jianji was known for pouring his family fortune into his men.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遣宦官韋令圖監其軍，令圖言：「建及得士心，懼有異志，不可令典牙兵。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Wei Lingtu to supervise his army. Lingtu said: “Jianji has won the soldiers’ hearts—I fear he may have other ambitions; he must not be allowed to command the guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Wei Lingtu to watch his army. Lingtu reported: “Jianji owns the soldiers’ hearts. I fear disloyalty. He must not keep command of the guard.

sentences.zh: 」即以為代州刺史。

translations.literal: ” He was then appointed prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” Jianji was transferred to prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 建及怏怏而卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Jianji died in resentment at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji died bitter at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 元行欽

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin

sentences.zh: 元行欽，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin was a native of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin came from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 為劉守光裨將，守光篡其父仁恭，使行欽以兵攻仁恭於大安山而囚之，又使行欽害諸兄弟。

translations.literal: He was Liu Shouguang’s lieutenant general. Shouguang usurped his father Renrong and sent Xingqin with troops to attack Renrong at Mount Da’an and imprison him, and also had Xingqin kill the brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liu Shouguang as lieutenant. When Shouguang overthrew his father Renrong, he sent Xingqin to besiege Renrong on Mount Da’an and take him prisoner, then had Xingqin kill the brothers one by one.

sentences.zh: 其後晉攻幽州，守光使行欽募兵雲、朔間。

translations.literal: Later when Jin attacked Youzhou, Shouguang sent Xingqin to raise troops between Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin later attacked Youzhou, Shouguang sent Xingqin to raise troops in Yun and Shuo.

sentences.zh: 是時明宗掠地山北，與行欽相拒廣邊軍，凡八戰，明宗七射中行欽，行欽拔矢而戰，亦射明宗中股。

translations.literal: At that time Mingzong was seizing lands north of the mountains and opposed Xingqin at Guangbian Army. In eight battles, Mingzong seven times hit Xingqin with arrows. Xingqin pulled out the arrows and fought on, and also shot Mingzong in the thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was then carving out territory north of the mountains and met Xingqin at Guangbian Army. They fought eight times. Seven arrows found Xingqin; each time he pulled them out and kept fighting, and once he put an arrow in Mingzong’s thigh.

sentences.zh: 行欽屢敗，乃降。

translations.literal: Xingqin lost repeatedly and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats Xingqin surrendered.

sentences.zh: 明宗撫其背而飲以酒曰：「壯士也！

translations.literal: Mingzong stroked his back and gave him wine, saying: “A true warrior!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong clapped his back and poured him wine: “Now that is a man!

sentences.zh: 」因養以為子。

translations.literal: ” He then adopted him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then he took him as an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 常從明宗戰，數立功。

translations.literal: He often followed Mingzong into battle and won merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Mingzong’s side again and again and won merit many times.

sentences.zh: 莊宗已下魏，益選驍將自衛，聞行欽驍勇，取之為散員都部署，賜姓名曰李紹榮。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong took Wei, he selected more fierce generals for personal guard. Hearing of Xingqin’s valor, he took him as chief of the scattered guard units and granted him the surname and name Li Shaorong.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong took Wei he gathered more fierce men for his personal guard. Hearing of Xingqin’s courage, he made him chief of the scattered guard and gave him the name Li Shaorong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗好戰而輕敵，與梁軍戰潘張，軍敗而潰，莊宗得三四騎馳去，梁兵數百追及，攢槊圍之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong loved battle and despised the enemy. Fighting Liang at Panzhang, the army was defeated and fled. Zhuangzong escaped with three or four horsemen; hundreds of Liang troops caught up and surrounded him with spears.
