translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong loved the fight and scorned his foes. At Panzhang the army broke. He fled with three or four riders while hundreds of Liang soldiers closed in and ringed him with spears.

sentences.zh: 行欽望其旗而識之，馳一騎，奪劍斷其二矛，斬首一級，梁兵解去。

translations.literal: Xingqin recognized Zhuangzong’s banner, rode alone, seized a sword and cut two spears, took one head, and the Liang troops dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin spotted Zhuangzong’s banner, charged alone, snatched a sword, snapped two spears, took a head, and the Liang ring broke apart.

sentences.zh: 莊宗還營，持行欽泣曰：「富貴與卿共之！

translations.literal: Returning to camp, Zhuangzong clasped Xingqin and wept: “Wealth and honor I will share with you!
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp Zhuangzong seized Xingqin and wept: “Whatever fortune comes, you and I share it!

sentences.zh: 」由是寵絕諸將。

translations.literal: ” From then on he was favored above all other generals.
translations.idiomatic: ” After that no general stood higher in his favor.

sentences.zh: 拜忻州刺史，遷武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Xinzhou and transferred to military governor of Wuning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Xinzhou, then military governor of Wuning Circuit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗宴群臣於內殿，酒酣樂作，道平生戰陣事以為笑樂，而怪行欽不在，因左右顧視曰：「紹榮安在？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong feasted his ministers in the inner hall. Wine deep, music playing, he talked of his battles with laughter—and wondered why Xingqin was not there. He looked around and said: “Where is Shaorong?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong feasted his ministers in the inner hall. Wine flowed, music rose, and he laughed over old battles—then noticed Xingqin was missing. He glanced about and asked: “Where is Shaorong?

sentences.zh: 」所司奏曰：「奉敕宴使相，紹榮散官，不得與也。

translations.literal: ” The officials reported: “By imperial decree the feast is for ministers; Shaorong is a scattered-rank officer and may not attend.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officials answered: “Your Majesty’s feast is for ministers. Shaorong holds scattered rank and may not enter.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗罷會不樂。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong ended the feast in displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong broke off the feast in a black mood.

sentences.zh: 明日，即拜行欽同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The next day he immediately made Xingqin Co-Emperor Secretary and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he made Xingqin co-chancellor on the spot.

sentences.zh: 自此不召群臣入內殿，但宴武臣而已。

translations.literal: From then on he no longer summoned ministers to the inner hall—only military officers were feasted.
translations.idiomatic: After that he stopped calling ministers into the inner hall and feasted only his warriors.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮反於魏，莊宗方選大將擊之，劉皇后曰：「此小事，可趣紹榮指揮。

translations.literal: Zhao Zaili rebelled at Wei. Zhuangzong was just selecting a great general to attack. Empress Liu said: “This is a small matter—send Shaorong at once to command.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rebelled at Wei, Zhuangzong was choosing a great general to crush him. Empress Liu said: “This is nothing—send Shaorong at once.

sentences.zh: 」乃以為鄴都行營招撫使，將二千人討之。

translations.literal: ” He was made pacification commissioner of the Ye capital campaign, leading two thousand men to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xingqin was made pacification commissioner for the Ye capital campaign with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 行欽攻鄴南門，以詔書招在禮。

translations.literal: Xingqin attacked the south gate of Ye and summoned Zaili with an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin struck Ye’s south gate and called Zaili down with an imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 在禮送羊酒犒軍，登城謂行欽曰：「將士經年離去父母，不取敕旨奔歸，上貽聖憂，追悔何及？

translations.literal: Zaili sent sheep and wine to reward the army, mounted the wall and said to Xingqin: “The soldiers have been away from their parents for years. They returned without imperial order and have troubled His Majesty—regret comes too late.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili sent sheep and wine to the camp, climbed the wall, and told Xingqin: “These men have been torn from their parents for years. They came home without leave and have shamed the throne. Regret is useless now.

sentences.zh: 若公善為之辭，尚能改過自新。

translations.literal: If you would speak well for us, we can still reform.
translations.idiomatic: Speak for us with kindness and we can still make amends.

sentences.zh: 」行欽曰：「天子以汝等有社稷之功，小過必當赦宥。

translations.literal: ” Xingqin said: “The Son of Heaven, considering your service to the realm, will surely pardon small faults.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xingqin said: “The emperor remembers your service to the realm. A small fault will surely be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 」在禮再拜，以詔書示諸軍。

translations.literal: ” Zaili bowed twice and showed the edict to the army.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zaili bowed low and displayed the edict to the troops.

sentences.zh: 皇甫暉從旁奪詔書壞之，軍士大噪。

translations.literal: Huangfu Hui snatched the edict from the side and tore it up; the soldiers roared.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Hui snatched the edict beside him and ripped it apart. The soldiers erupted.

sentences.zh: 行欽具以聞，莊宗大怒，敕行欽：「破城之日，無遺種！

translations.literal: Xingqin reported everything. Zhuangzong was furious and ordered Xingqin: “When the city falls, leave no one alive!
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin reported all of it. Zhuangzong raged and commanded: “When the walls fall, spare no one!

sentences.zh: 」乃益召諸鎮兵，皆屬行欽。

translations.literal: ” More troops were summoned from every circuit and placed under Xingqin.
translations.idiomatic: ” More troops were called from every circuit and put under Xingqin.

sentences.zh: 行欽屯澶州，分諸鎮兵為五道，毀民車輪、門扉、屋椽為筏，渡長慶河攻冠氏門，不克。

translations.literal: Xingqin encamped at Cao prefecture, divided the circuit troops into five columns, tore up cart wheels, doors, and roof beams to make rafts, crossed the Changqing River and attacked the Guanshi Gate, but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin camped at Cao, split the circuit armies into five columns, ripped cart wheels, doors, and rafters into rafts, crossed the Changqing River, and struck the Guanshi Gate—but failed.

sentences.zh: 是時，邢、洺諸州，相繼皆叛，而行欽攻鄴無功，莊宗欲自將以往，群臣皆諫止，乃遣明宗討之。

translations.literal: By then Xing and Ming circuits had rebelled one after another, yet Xingqin’s assault on Ye had no success. Zhuangzong wished to lead the army himself; the ministers all remonstrated and stopped him, and Mingzong was sent to suppress the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Xing and Ming had already risen in turn while Xingqin battered Ye without result. Zhuangzong wanted to go in person. The ministers talked him out of it and sent Mingzong instead.

sentences.zh: 明宗至魏，軍城西，行欽軍城南。

translations.literal: Mingzong reached Wei and encamped west of the city; Xingqin encamped south of it.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong reached Wei and camped west of the walls. Xingqin sat south of the city.

sentences.zh: 而明宗軍變，入於魏，與在禮合。

translations.literal: Then Mingzong’s army mutinied, entered Wei, and joined Zaili.
translations.idiomatic: Then Mingzong’s army turned, marched into Wei, and joined Zaili.

sentences.zh: 行欽聞之，退屯衛州，以明宗反聞。

translations.literal: When Xingqin heard this, he withdrew to Weizhou and reported Mingzong’s rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqin heard the news, pulled back to Weizhou, and reported that Mingzong had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遣金槍指揮使李從璟馳詔明宗計事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong sent Golden Spear commander Li Congjing with an urgent edict to consult Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sent Golden Spear commander Li Congjing with an urgent edict to parley with Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 從璟，明宗子也。

translations.literal: Congjing was Mingzong’s son.
translations.idiomatic: Congjing was Mingzong’s son.

sentences.zh: 行至衛州，而明宗已反，行欽乃系從璟，將殺之，從璟請還京師，乃許之。

translations.literal: When he reached Weizhou, Mingzong had already rebelled. Xingqin bound Congjing and was about to kill him; Congjing asked to return to the capital, and Xingqin allowed it.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou Mingzong had already turned. Xingqin seized Congjing and meant to kill him. Congjing begged to return to the capital, and Xingqin let him go.

sentences.zh: 明宗自魏縣引兵南，行欽率兵趨還京師。

translations.literal: Mingzong led his army south from Wei county; Xingqin hurried back to the capital with his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong marched south from Wei county. Xingqin raced back to the capital with his men.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗幸汴州，行至滎澤，聞明宗已渡黎陽，莊宗復遣從璟通問於明宗，行欽以為不可，因擊殺從璟。

translations.literal: He followed Zhuangzong to Bian prefecture. At Xingze they heard Mingzong had crossed Liyang. Zhuangzong again sent Congjing to open talks with Mingzong; Xingqin said it must not be done and killed Congjing.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong east to Bian. At Xingze they learned Mingzong had crossed Liyang. Zhuangzong sent Congjing again to treat with Mingzong. Xingqin forbade it and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 明宗入汴州，莊宗至萬勝鎮，不得進，與行欽登道旁冢，置酒，相顧泣下。

translations.literal: Mingzong entered Bian. Zhuangzong reached Wansheng post station and could advance no farther. He and Xingqin climbed a roadside tomb mound, set out wine, and wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong entered Bian. Zhuangzong halted at Wansheng station and could go no farther. He and Xingqin climbed a tomb by the road, poured wine, and wept across the cups.

sentences.zh: 有野人獻雉，問其冢名，野人曰：「愁臺也。

translations.literal: A countryman brought a pheasant. Asked the tomb’s name, the man said: “It is the Mound of Grief.
translations.idiomatic: A countryman offered a pheasant. Asked the tomb’s name, he said: “The Mound of Grief.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗益不悅，因罷酒去。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong grew still more displeased and broke off the wine and left.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong’s mood darkened further. He stopped drinking and went on.

sentences.zh: 西至石橋，置酒野次，莊宗謂行欽曰：「卿等從我久，富貴急難無不同也。

translations.literal: West of Shiqiao he set wine in the open field. Zhuangzong said to Xingqin: “You have followed me long—wealth, peril, and hardship we have shared alike.
translations.idiomatic: West of Shiqiao he spread wine in the open field and said to Xingqin: “You have been with me for years. Fortune and danger alike we have shared.

sentences.zh: 今茲危蹙，而默默無言，坐視成敗。

translations.literal: Now crisis presses close, yet you are silent and watch success or failure as spectators.
translations.idiomatic: Now ruin closes in, and you sit mute, watching as though the outcome were not yours.

sentences.zh: 我至滎澤，欲單騎渡河，自求總管，卿等各陳利害。

translations.literal: When I reached Xingze I wanted to ride alone across the river and seek out the overall commander myself—each of you should have spoken your mind.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingze I meant to cross the river alone and throw myself on the overall commander. Each of you should have told me plainly what to do.

sentences.zh: 今日俾我至此，卿等何如？

translations.literal: Today you have brought me to this—what of it?
translations.idiomatic: Today you have brought me to this pass—what now?

sentences.zh: 」行欽泣而對曰：「臣本小人，蒙陛下撫養，位至將相。

translations.literal: ” Xingqin wept and answered: “Your servant is a common man whom Your Majesty raised to general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xingqin wept and answered: “I am a nobody Your Majesty raised to general and minister.

sentences.zh: 危難之時，不能報國，雖死無以塞責。

translations.literal: In this crisis I cannot repay the realm; even death would not settle my debt.
translations.idiomatic: In this crisis I cannot repay the state. Even if I die, my debt remains unpaid.

sentences.zh: 」因與諸將百餘人，皆解髻斷發，置之於地，誓以死報，君臣相持慟哭。

translations.literal: ” He and more than a hundred generals all unbound their hair, cut it off, laid it on the ground, and swore to die in service. Ruler and ministers clung to one another and wept.
translations.idiomatic: ” He and more than a hundred officers unbound their hair, cut it off, laid the locks on the ground, and swore to die for him. Emperor and men held one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 莊宗還洛陽，數日，復幸汜水。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong returned to Luoyang; several days later he again went to Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong went back to Luoyang. Days later he set out again for Sishui.

sentences.zh: 郭從謙反，莊宗崩，行欽出奔。

translations.literal: Guo Congqian rebelled; Zhuangzong fell. Xingqin fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congqian rebelled. Zhuangzong died. Xingqin ran.

sentences.zh: 行至平陸，為野人所執，送虢州，刺史石潭折其兩足，載以檻車，送京師。

translations.literal: At Pinglu he was seized by country people, sent to Guo prefecture; prefect Shi Tan broke both his legs, loaded him in a cage cart, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Pinglu country folk seized him and sent him to Guo prefecture. Prefect Shi Tan broke both his legs, put him in a cage cart, and shipped him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明宗見之，罵曰：「我兒何負於爾！

translations.literal: When Mingzong saw him he cursed: “What wrong did my son do you!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong saw him and cursed: “What did my son ever do to you!

sentences.zh: 」行欽瞋目直視曰：「先皇帝何負於爾！

translations.literal: ” Xingqin glared straight at him and said: “What wrong did the late emperor do you!
translations.idiomatic: ” Xingqin stared back and said: “What did the late emperor ever do to you!

sentences.zh: 」乃斬於洛陽市，市人皆為之流涕。

translations.literal: ” He was executed in the Luoyang market; the townspeople all wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was beheaded in the Luoyang market, and the crowd wept.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 死之所以可貴者，以其義不茍生爾。

translations.literal: Death is prized because one refuses to live at the cost of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Death is honored when a man will not buy life at the price of duty.

sentences.zh: 故曰：主在與在，主亡與亡者，社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: Hence the saying: “When the lord lives, I live; when the lord dies, I die”—such men are ministers of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes: “While the lord lives, I live; when the lord dies, I die”—that is a minister of the realm.

sentences.zh: 方明宗之兵變於魏，諸將未知去就，而行欽獨以反聞，又殺其子從璟，至於斷發自誓，其誠節有足嘉矣。

translations.literal: When Mingzong’s army mutinied at Wei, the generals did not yet know where to stand, yet Xingqin alone reported rebellion, killed his son Congjing, and even cut his hair in oath—his loyalty in that hour deserves praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong’s army turned at Wei, other generals still wavered, yet Xingqin alone cried rebellion, killed Congjing, and cut his hair in oath. In that hour his loyalty deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗之崩，不能自決，而反逃死以求生，終於被執而見殺。

translations.literal: Yet when Zhuangzong fell, he could not resolve to die and instead fled to live—until he was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Zhuangzong fell he could not choose death and ran instead—until capture and execution found him.

sentences.zh: 其言雖不屈，而死非其志也，烏足貴哉！

translations.literal: Though his words did not bend, his death was not what he had sworn—how can it be prized?
translations.idiomatic: His tongue stayed stiff, but his death was not the death he had sworn. What is there to honor?

sentences.zh: 安金全

translations.literal: An Jinquan
translations.idiomatic: An Jinquan

sentences.zh: 袁建豐

translations.literal: Yuan Jianfeng
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jianfeng

sentences.zh: 西方鄴

translations.literal: Xi Fangye
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fangye

sentences.zh: 西方鄴，定州滿城人也。

translations.literal: Xi Fangye was a native of Mancheng in Ding prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fangye came from Mancheng in Ding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父再遇，為汴州軍校，鄴居軍中，以勇力聞。

translations.literal: His father Zaiyu was a Bianzhou army officer; Fangye grew up in the army and was known for courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zaiyu served as an officer at Bianzhou. Fangye was raised in camp and became known for raw strength.

sentences.zh: 年二十，南渡河遊梁，不見用，復歸莊宗於河上，莊宗以為孝義指揮使，數從征伐有功，同光中為曹州刺史，以州兵屯汴州。

translations.literal: At twenty he crossed the river south to seek service in Liang but found no post; he returned to Zhuangzong on the river line. Zhuangzong made him drill commissioner of Xiaoyi, and he followed campaigns with repeated merit. In the Tongguang era he was prefect of Cao and stationed his prefectural troops at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he crossed south to Liang and found no place. He went back to Zhuangzong on the river and was made drill commissioner of Xiaoyi. He fought in campaign after campaign and won merit. Under Tongguang he became prefect of Cao and kept his troops at Bian.

sentences.zh: 明宗自魏反，兵南渡河，而莊宗東幸汴州，汴州節度使孔循懷二誌，使北門迎明宗，西門迎莊宗，所以供帳委積如一，曰：「先至者入之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong rebelled from Wei and led his army south across the river, Zhuangzong went east to Bian. Bian’s military governor Kong Xun held two minds: he ordered the north gate to welcome Mingzong and the west gate to welcome Zhuangzong, preparing supplies and stores alike for both, saying: “Whoever arrives first may enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong turned at Wei and marched south across the river, Zhuangzong went east to Bian. Kong Xun, military governor of Bian, hedged his bets: the north gate would welcome Mingzong, the west gate Zhuangzong. He stocked both camps the same and said: “Whoever comes first gets the city.

sentences.zh: 」鄴因責循曰：「主上破梁而得公，有不殺之恩，奈何欲納總管而負國！

translations.literal: ” Fangye rebuked Xun: “Your Majesty destroyed Liang and spared you—how can you mean to admit the overall commander and betray the realm!
translations.idiomatic: ” Fangye rounded on Xun: “The emperor broke Liang and spared your life. How can you mean to hand the city to the overall commander and betray the throne!

sentences.zh: 」循不答。

translations.literal: ” Xun did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xun said nothing.

sentences.zh: 鄴度循不可爭，而石敬瑭妻，明宗女也，時方在汴，鄴欲殺之，以堅人心。

translations.literal: Fangye judged that Xun could not be moved. Shi Jingtang’s wife was Mingzong’s daughter and was then at Bian; Fangye wished to kill her to stiffen the men’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Fangye saw Xun would not be moved. Shi Jingtang’s wife—Mingzong’s daughter—was then in Bian. Fangye meant to kill her and harden the army’s resolve.

sentences.zh: 循知其謀，取藏其家，鄴無如之何。

translations.literal: Xun learned of his plan, took her and hid her in his household, and Fangye could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun learned what Fangye meant to do, took the princess into his own house and hid her—and Fangye could not touch her.

sentences.zh: 而明宗已及汴，乃將五百騎西迎莊宗於汜水，嗚咽泣下，莊宗亦為之噓唏，乃使以兵為先鋒。

translations.literal: By then Mingzong had already reached Bian; Fangye then led five hundred cavalry west to welcome Zhuangzong at Si River, sobbing with tears streaming down; Zhuangzong also wept in response and had them serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong had already reached Bian. Fangye led five hundred horsemen west to meet Zhuangzong at Si River, weeping so hard he could barely speak; Zhuangzong wept with him and put his men in the van.

sentences.zh: 慶宗至汴西，不得入，還洛陽，遇弒。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong reached west of Bian but could not enter; he returned to Luoyang and met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong came to the west of Bian and could not get in. He turned back to Luoyang—and there met his death.

sentences.zh: 明宗入洛，鄴請死於馬前，明宗嘉嘆久之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Fangye asked to die before his horse; Mingzong praised and sighed over him at length.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, Fangye begged to die beneath his horse. Mingzong praised him long and deeply, and sighed.

sentences.zh: 明年，荊南高季興叛，明宗遣襄州節度使劉訓等招討，而以東川董璋為西南面招討使，乃拜鄴夔州刺史，副璋以兵出三峽。

translations.literal: The next year Gao Jixing of Jingnan rebelled; Mingzong sent Liu Xun, military governor of Xiangzhou, and others as suppression commissioners, and made Dong Zhang of Dongchuan southwest suppression commissioner. Fangye was then appointed prefect of Qizhou, to serve under Zhang and lead troops out through the Three Gorges.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Gao Jixing of Jingnan rebelled. Mingzong sent Liu Xun of Xiangzhou and others to suppress him, made Dong Zhang of Dongchuan southwest suppression commissioner, and named Fangye prefect of Qizhou to serve under Zhang and march out through the Three Gorges.

sentences.zh: 已而訓等無功見黜，諸將皆罷，璋亦嘗出兵，惟鄴獨取三州，乃以夔州為寧江軍，拜鄴節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Xun and the others, having achieved nothing, were removed; all the generals were dismissed. Zhang had also marched once, but only Fangye alone took the three prefectures. Qizhou was then made the Ningjiang army, and Fangye was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun and the rest failed and were cashiered; every other commander was pulled back. Zhang had marched, but only Fangye took Qizhou, Zhongzhou, and Wanzhou on his own. The court then made Qizhou the seat of the Ningjiang army and Fangye its military governor.

sentences.zh: 已而又取歸州，數敗季興之兵。

translations.literal: Later he also took Guizhou and repeatedly defeated Gao Jixing’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: He took Guizhou afterward and beat Gao Jixing’s armies again and again.

sentences.zh: 鄴武人，所為多不中法度，判官譚善達數以諫。

translations.literal: Fangye was a military man; much of what he did fell outside the law. His magistrate Tan Shanda remonstrated with him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Fangye was a soldier through and through, and his conduct often ignored the law. Magistrate Tan Shanda warned him again and again.

sentences.zh: 鄴怒，遣人告善達受人金，下獄。

translations.literal: Fangye grew angry, sent men to accuse Shanda of taking bribes, and had him thrown in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fangye flew into a rage, had Shanda denounced for taking bribes, and threw him in jail.

sentences.zh: 善達素剛，辭益不遜，遂死於獄中。

translations.literal: Shanda had always been fierce; his words grew ever more insolent, and he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shanda had always been unyielding. The more they pressed him, the sharper his answers grew—until he died in his cell.

sentences.zh: 鄴病，見善達為祟，卒於鎮。

translations.literal: Fangye fell ill, saw Shanda haunting him, and died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Fangye took sick, saw Shanda’s ghost tormenting him, and died in command.
